## What `src/billing.ts` does

Billing module containing invoice generation and refund-preview logic. Key symbols:
- `generateInvoice` (lines 50–253) — the orchestrator
- `calculateRefundPreview` (lines 40–44) — named like a pure calculation but actually calls `saveRefundAudit` and `sendRefundEmail`

The file is 310 lines with 5 top-level functions, uses `Date.now()`/`new Date()` directly in 7 places, and carries a load-bearing rule only in a comment: *"Only owners can refund enterprise plans unless billing support approves."*

## Related files to read before editing

**Shares the `"enterprise"` literal** (crime_00010) — edits to plan-tier logic likely need to touch these too:
- `src/api/plan.ts:2`
- `src/jobs/plan-sync.ts:2`
- `src/ui/pricing.ts:2`

**Routing/UI for billing** (crime_00015, crime_00017) — destination `/settings/billing` is labelled three different ways:
- `src/routes/settings/billing.tsx` (component `PricingPage`, title "Subscription")
- `src/nav/registry.ts` (label "Plans")
- `src/nav/sidebar.ts` (label "Billing")

**Tests** — `src/billing.test.ts` (weak: "renders the enterprise plan" asserts nothing; "creates an invoice" uses only weak matchers — don't trust them as a safety net)

**Docs** — `docs/billing.md` (in the `tenant`/`account`/`organisation`/`team`/`workspace` alias group; expect concept drift)

## Risks the scan flagged on this file

| Severity | Charge | Where | Why it matters for the edit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **high** | God Function | `generateInvoice` 50–253 (204 lines, 3.4× threshold) | Unrelated responsibilities mixed; easy to miss interactions |
| **medium** | God File | whole file, 310 lines | Local coupling hidden from an agent's loaded context |
| **medium** | Temporal Recklessness | lines 57, 63, 92, 198, 238, 250, 273 | Non-deterministic; tests can't pin time without monkey-patching |
| **medium** | False Identity | `calculateRefundPreview` 40–44 | Name implies pure, body has side effects — callers may treat it as safe |
| **medium** | Logic in the Alibi | line 39 (refund authorisation rule) | Owner/billing-support rule lives only in prose; no guard/type/test encodes it |
| **low** | Unfinished Business | lines 183, 308 (4 TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX) | Hard to tell which logic is load-bearing vs draft |

Two cross-file gotchas worth singling out before touching plan-tier code: the `"enterprise"` literal is duplicated across four files (any policy change has four edit sites), and the test file's two cases provide effectively no behavioural coverage — assume you're editing without a safety net.
